recommendations.rationale: Defer any tip-speed or terminal-braking weighting change: the completed update-34 braking-box check measured an endpoint tip speed of 0.6129798468327005 m/s against 0.6155277254823904 m/s for the recorded input over 0.01 s, so even a maximal local braking input leaves the endpoint speed far above the 0.02 m/s settling limit at this state, and no check here maps raw weights to cost-term importance or closed-loop settling. No production parameter change is in scope for this phase.

Defer conclusions about per-update plan selection and effective-horizon truncation: the recorded effective horizon at update 34 is 1 control interval with selected iteration index 31 and 35 recorded wall-clock deadline misses, but optimizer iteration traces and full warm plans are not retained (control_snapshots.json not retained), so this cannot be separated from objective weighting or projected-model mismatch.

Defer any claim about when or whether tip speed first fell below the 0.02 m/s limit until approach-phase samples (controller updates 0-26, sampled times 0.01-0.29 s) and their one-step predictions are read; displayed coverage here is controller updates 27-34 and sampled backend times 0.30-0.35 s only.

Defer a projected-model-versus-backend mismatch verdict: the check evaluates model.gvs@1.0.0 at one recorded projected state with an instantaneous affine-input assumption over a 10 ms horizon, and no closed-loop replay or causal-attribution capability exists to size how much of the settling failure that mismatch could carry.

attribution.reason: Observed failure mode rather than a cause assignment: inside the 0.05 s window the recorded tip speeds (late-window maximum 1.5810152739742807 m/s and terminal 0.6351726092425104 m/s) exceed the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit while position error is already inside 0.01 m, so the speed criterion was not met at any sampled point of the window even though position tracked well.

Within this bounded probe the braking-box arm drove two tendon entries to a recorded force margin of 0 N and showed an instantaneous velocity-direction deceleration far larger than the recorded arm's, yet its 0.01 s endpoint tip speed was only about 0.0025 m/s from the recorded arm's and remained far above the 0.02 m/s limit; i.e. at this saved state over 10 ms the recorded terminal input left negligible endpoint speed authority unused. Scope: one saved projected state, projected model, five integration steps.

The check hypothesis that an instantaneous braking-box input yields a materially lower endpoint tip speed than the recorded actual_tension_n is contradicted at this state and horizon: the measured endpoint speed difference is about 0.0025 m/s on a scale where the recorded endpoint speed is 0.6155277254823904 m/s and the settling limit is 0.02 m/s. Ruled out only for this single saved projected state over 0.01 s on model.gvs@1.0.0; it is not a statement about the recorded plan over the full horizon or about other saved states.

The braking arm ended with a larger recorded endpoint tip error (0.009868288776480223 m) than the recorded arm's last displayed error (0.007780986611465467 m, at 0.008 s) while its position drift was smaller, which is consistent with a position-speed trade in the direction of slightly worse endpoint position for essentially no speed gain; however the recorded arm's 0.01 s endpoint position/error is not displayed, so the arm-to-arm endpoint position difference is not established and the trade cannot be quantified.

The recorded weights are speed-light (terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001 against tracking_weight 1.0 and terminal_weight 5.0) and the local probe shows almost no endpoint speed change from a maximal braking-box input at the update-34 state, which is consistent with a speed-light objective; but raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance, no cost contributions or scaling are retained, the probe applies one fixed input over 10 ms rather than re-solving the multi-interval objective with a single adopted weight change, and no closed-loop comparison exists, so this candidate cannot be separated from plan selection / horizon compression or from projected-model mismatch.

Recorded effective horizon at update 34 was 1 control interval with selected iteration index 31, and the run recorded 35 wall-clock deadline misses, which is compatible with budget-limited plan selection over the late window; but previously displayed late updates recorded plan_accepted=true with decreasing error, and optimizer iteration traces and full warm plans are not retained, so this candidate remains possible but unranked against objective weighting or model mismatch.

This check evaluates model.gvs@1.0.0 at a recorded projected GVS state with an instantaneous affine-input assumption, so it bounds neither the serial backend's true behaviour nor the recorded predicted-versus-measured endpoint differences; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot explain an entire settling failure, and no closed-loop replay or causal-attribution tool exists to size that mismatch.

The recorded 35 deadline misses and mean update wall time of 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period describe wall-clock scheduling of synchronous controller calls; under the host scheduling contract those calls complete before fixed-count backend steps, so wall latency does not inject physical delay into simulated time and cannot itself be the mechanism of the physical settling failure (it remains relevant only as a possible contributor to truncated optimization, the plan-selection candidate).

facts.statement: At the saved update-34 projected state over the fixed 0.01 s horizon (model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit Euler in mass/force form, 0.002 s step), the recorded-input arm ended at tip speed 0.6155277254823904 m/s and the instantaneous braking-box arm ended at 0.6129798468327005 m/s; the two endpoint speeds differ by only about 0.0025 m/s (a rounded arithmetic difference of two retrieved values, not a new computation) and both remain far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

At the same state and horizon the braking-box arm recorded endpoint force margins of 0 N N on the third and fourth of six tendon entries and 8 N on the remaining four, and its recorded velocity-direction deceleration of 891.7363309396493 m/s^2 compares with 22.297467181011292 m/s^2 for the recorded-input arm, whose applied tension was [3.1758909392099772, 2.757372796476204, 1.4216485070827969e-08, 0.8929758192138912, 0.12734806870748366, 0.0] N.

At the same horizon the braking-box arm's endpoint tip position error was 0.009868288776480223 m with position drift 0.004113715254212544 m, versus a recorded-input arm position drift of 0.006487739485323485 m; the recorded-input arm's own 0.01 s endpoint position/error is not in the displayed catalog (its last displayed error is 0.007780986611465467 m at the 0.008 s rollout step), so an arm-to-arm endpoint position difference cannot be read off directly.

Both checked arms start from the same retrieved recorded projected state with tip velocity [0.1785677504675266, -0.31310195705869154, -0.6572579477056314] m/s and tip error 0.009247332035268509 m at rollout time 0.0 s; the probe definition is -v_tip.T @ (J qdd + Jdot qdot) / ||v_tip||, its search is an analytic bounded linear objective on a unilateral tension box with no iterative input optimizer, and its state scope is the recorded projected GVS state, not the complete backend state. Inputs are taken from the recorded /34/actual_tension_n and /34/measured_initial_state pointers.

Retained record context: reach passed with terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance, sampled settling failed against a 0.02 m/s speed limit over a 0.05 s window, recorded terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s, late-window maximum tip speed 1.5810152739742807 m/s, late-window maximum error 0.05813810428573256 m.

Recorded controller evidence: update 34 had effective horizon 1 control interval and selected optimization iteration index 31; the run recorded 35 deadline misses with mean update wall time 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period; recorded recipe weights are tracking_weight 1.0, terminal_weight 5.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001 and tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02.

limitations: This revision rests on one completed saved-state check at a single saved projected state (update 34) over 0.01 s, plus retained records previously read in this context for controller updates 27-34 and sampled backend times 0.30-0.35 s; it is a bounded comparison, not a closed-loop result.

Model limit: the probe uses model.gvs@1.0.0 with implicit Euler in mass/force form (0.002 s step, five steps) and an instantaneous affine-input acceleration definition at fixed recorded pose/rate, applied to the recorded projected GVS state and not to the complete serial backend state; it is a model-predicted possibility, not an experimental braking claim.

Input limit: the braking arm is a single instantaneous unilateral-box input, not a re-solve of the multi-interval objective with one adopted weight change, so it measures local input authority at one state rather than objective weighting or plan selection.

Horizon limit: a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot explain an entire settling failure; the retained terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s and late-window maximum 1.5810152739742807 m/s are not altered by this probe and remain the recorded failure signature.

Coverage limit: only update 34 was evaluated under the max_checks=1 grant; controller updates 0-26 and the approach phase (sampled backend times 0.01-0.29 s) were not read in this context, and other late-window saved states (e.g. updates 32 and 33) were not evaluated, so the update-34 result is not generalized across the run.

Capability limit: no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability exists, and historical optimizer iteration traces and full warm plans are not retained (control_snapshots.json), so the recorded effective-horizon compression cannot be attributed to budget truncation rather than objective weighting.
Raw recipe weight magnitudes are reported as recorded configuration and do not establish cost-term importance without actual cost contributions or scaling, which are not retained.

The recorded prediction-versus-measurement velocity differences mix two definitions (directly recorded accepted first-step endpoint velocity versus reconstructed J_site(q_backend) @ qdot_backend), so they bound rather than measure backend-model mismatch.
Single execution; no further check is authorized in this phase.
